chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ayn, who said:

I said to him, 'The wife of Abd al-Malik gave birth, so he counted for her the days of her menstruation, then he ordered her to perform ghusl and insert a cloth (for istihada), and he ordered her to wear two clean garments, and he ordered her to perform salat. She said to him, 'I do not feel comfortable entering the mosque, so let me stand outside of it and prostrate within it.'

He said, 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had ordered with it, and said: When the blood ceases from the woman and she sees purity.' And Ali (peace be upon him) had ordered with this before you: 'When the blood ceases from the woman and she sees purity.' So what did your companion do? I said, 'I do not know.'

key_terms.صَاحِبَتُكُمْ: Your companion (referring to the wife of Abd al-Malik)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who continues to bleed after childbirth and how should she perform prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between post-childbirth bleeding (nafsāʾ) and irregular bleeding (istihāḍah), establishing that the cessation of blood flow, rather than a fixed duration, triggers the obligation of ghusl and resumption of prayer. It highlights the practical flexibility granted to women, allowing them to pray outside the mosque if they feel unclean, while affirming the continuity of this ruling from the Prophet and Imam Ali (peace be upon him). The narrative underscores the Shia emphasis on observable purity signs over rigid temporal limits in personal status law.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Ayn who said,

‘I said to himasws, ‘The wife of Abdul Malik gave birth. So he counted for her the days of her menstruation (Haydh), then instructed her to wash and insert a cloth, and he instructed her that she should wear two (layers of) clean clothes, and instructed her with the Salaat. So, she said to him, ‘I do not feel good for myself that I should enter the Masjid, therefore leave me to stand outside from it, and I shall prostrate therein’’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> had ordered with it and said: ‘If the blood gets cut off from the woman and she sees the purity (so she can enter the Masjid)’, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> had ordered with this before you: ‘If the blood gets cut off from the woman and she sees the cleanliness (so she can enter the Masjid)’. So what did your companion do?’ I said, ‘I do not know’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ’A‘yan who has said the following:

“I once said to him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that the wife of ‘Abd al-Malik gave birth. He instructed her to wait for the number of days of her Hayd (menses), then instructed her to take Ghusl (bath), fill up, wear two clean clothes and perform Salah (prayer). She said, ‘My soul does not feel happy to enter the Masjid; so allow me to stay out of the Masjid and prostrate in it.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘The Messenger of Allah had issued such commandments and said, ‘Bleeding stops and she finds cleanliness,’ and Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, before you had issued such commandments; once bleeding stops the woman finds herself clean. What did the woman (of your companion) do?’ I replied, ‘I do not know.’” (‘Abd al-Malik mentioned is perhaps ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ’A‘yan, according to al-Dhakhirah).
